summary: When Lot was captured, Abram rescued him. Afterward, the priest-king Melchizedek blessed Abram, and Abram refused riches from the king of Sodom so everyone would know God had blessed him.

story_reel.narration: One day, a messenger ran to Abram with bad news. Four kings had attacked the cities in the valley, and they had captured Lot and taken everything he owned! Abram didn't hesitate. He gathered 318 trained men from his household and chased after the kings all the way to the north. At night, Abram's men surprised the enemy, rescued Lot, and brought back all the people and their belongings. On the way home, a mysterious king named Melchizedek came out to meet Abram. He was king of Salem and a priest of God Most High. He brought bread and wine and blessed Abram: 'Blessed be Abram by God Most High, maker of heaven and earth!' Abram gave Melchizedek a tenth of everything. Then the king of Sodom said, 'Keep all the riches for yourself.' But Abram said, 'No, I won't take even a thread or a sandal strap. I don't want anyone to say a king made me rich.' Abram knew that everything he had came from God.

scenes.caption: 318 brave men

memory_verse.text: The earth is Yahweh's, with its fullness; the world, and those who dwell in it.
tokens: and those who dwell in it.

identity_focus.core_truth: My things are all gifts from Yahweh, and I can use them to help others.
identity_focus.reflection_prompt: Abram rushed to help Lot when he was in trouble. Who is someone you could help or stick up for?
reflection_choices: A friend who is being teased
Someone who needs help with something

quiz.question: How many trained men did Abram take to rescue Lot?
quiz.explanation: Abram led out his 318 trained men, born in his house.

quiz.question: What did Melchizedek bring to Abram?
quiz.explanation: Melchizedek, king of Salem and priest of God Most High, brought out bread and wine.

quiz.question: Why did Abram refuse the king of Sodom's riches?
options: So no one could say a king made him rich
quiz.explanation: Abram said he wouldn't take anything so the king couldn't say, 'I have made Abram rich.'

micro_prayer.text: Yahweh, everything I have comes from You. Thank You for every gift. Help me be brave to help others, and help me remember that You are the One who blesses me. Amen.

companion.message: Abram could have kept all those riches. But he wanted everyone to know his blessings came from Yahweh. That's a lesson I learned in Egypt too.

review.notes: Mentions a rescue raid (Genesis 14:15); no battle shown or described beyond 'surprised the enemy.' Confirm tone.
